Ride-hailing licence applications open
body:
The Transport Department (TD) today invited interested platform companies to apply for ride-hailing service licences.

 

If an applicant company’s licence application is approved, the licence will be valid for a maximum period of five years, with an annual licence fee of HK$1.2 million.

 

The Government said that to ensure ride-hailing platforms have the operational capability to provide these services, it will impose certain requirements in areas such as booking management technology, operational experience, and proof of financial capability and capital investment.

 

Firstly, applicants must be companies registered in Hong Kong and maintain a permanent establishment of executive personnel and an office in Hong Kong to facilitate government regulation.

 

Applicant companies must demonstrate their scale of operations, including lawful operation in a city with a population comparable to Hong Kong's – 7.5 million or above.

 

In at least two cities where ride-hailing platform services are provided, the daily average number of orders processed in each city must reach 100,000 or more.

 

Additionally, applicant companies must demonstrate their financial capability to support the stable operation of their platforms in Hong Kong to provide proper and efficient services continuously.

 

Apart from filing audited financial reports for the past three years, applicants should possess no less than HK$50 million in company paid-up capital, and at least HK$30 million each in bank deposits and credit facilities.

 

Applicant companies must also submit a proposal detailing their service plans, such as corporate management, customer service, and due diligence to ensure compliance with owner-driver binding requirements.

 

Interested companies registered in Hong Kong may request invitation documents through the TD’s website. 

 

Additionally, the TD is developing a ride-hailing vehicle data management system to receive operational data in real time. Such data will help the Government regulate ride-hailing services, understand actual operations, and conduct dynamic assessments for future policy reviews.

 

The application closes at noon on October 30.

title: AI-powered 1823 upgrades
body:
The Digital Policy Office (DPO) has announced the launch of four AI Efficacy Enhancement Projects, an initiative led by the AI Efficacy Enhancement Team to upgrade 1823 public services.

 

Among these is Call Assistant, which leverages speech recognition technology and large language models (LLMs) to transcribe phone conversations on designated topics in real time, automatically generating concise summaries to reduce post-call administrative work by 15%. 

 

Simultaneously, Email Extraction utilises an LLM to analyse incoming public emails, automatically extracting key case details and populating the customer service management system to cut manual data entry time by an estimated 30%.

 

To streamline urgent matters, Prioritisation of Departments' Replies applies AI algorithms to analyse email content and flag high-priority cases, with identification time expected to shorten from two days to just a few hours. 

 

Finally, the Dashboard initiative leverages AI to consolidate and present case data, enabling departments to follow up on local issues and strengthen district governance.

 

Additionally, the DPO plans to launch the 1823 web application on the iAM Smart platform in the fourth quarter to replace the existing 1823 mobile app, allowing the public to access 1823 services directly through the iAM Smart platform.

 

The DPO is also providing all-round support for departments in adopting AI to drive public service transformation.

 

The Government Cloud Infrastructure Services, which currently supports over 60 bureaus and departments and 600 digital government services, provides private cloud services, shared advanced AI computing power, LLMs and AI development tools, enabling departments to develop digital and smart government services more reliably and flexibly.

 

Furthermore, the DPO will develop two innovative AI services: the iAM Smart AI Assistant, which allows the public to ask questions and instantly receive information and related service links from the app, and AI Agents, which assist government personnel in handling standardised and repetitive administrative tasks using intelligent AI.

 

Acting Commissioner for Digital Policy Daniel Cheung noted at a briefing that AI is rapidly transforming the mode of public services.

 

“The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government is actively driving an AI+ public service transformation to enhance government efficiency and optimise citizens’ user experience with AI," Mr Cheung said.

 

“The DPO will spearhead and provide support in the process, assisting various departments in adopting AI safely and effectively,” he said.

title: CE visits Sham Shui Po
body:
Chief Executive John Lee today toured a public housing estate, an elderly centre and the 1823 Contact Centre in Sham Shui Po District to hear the public’s views ahead of the 2026 Policy Address.

  

During his visit to Un Chau Estate, Mr Lee met an elderly resident to learn about her experience with ambulatory care services. He noted that the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government has been actively promoting these services, which allow suitable patients to undergo examinations and treatments with multidisciplinary support, enabling them to rest at home without the need for overnight hospital stays.

 

Ambulatory care services help reduce unnecessary hospitalisation and provide patients with more convenient treatment and services. Mr Lee added that this could enhance the service capacity and efficiency of the public healthcare system, while allowing more people to receive appropriate services at an early stage.

 

Earlier, the Chief Executive visited Kwong Wah Hospital to review the operation of its Ambulatory Orthopaedic Service Centre and its deployment of innovative technologies. He said the Hong Kong SAR Government is committed to deepening healthcare reform and enhancing service quality, particularly through the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to improve the accuracy and speed of clinical diagnoses.

 

Following the public estate tour, Mr Lee proceeded to the Un Chau Estate Baptist Church Elderly Centre to observe its activities and support services. Mr Lee said the Government has long upheld ageing in place as a core principle, and has continued to strengthen elderly support, including increasing the total number of Community Care Service Vouchers for the Elderly, and establishing three Neighbourhood Elderly Centres as announced in last year’s Policy Address.

 

The Chief Executive then visited the 1823 Contact Centre to observe how it leverages AI to expedite public enquiries, assistance requests and complaints. He said the centre’s active application of AI in receiving cases, data analysis and workflow assignments has enabled it to respond more quickly to assistance requests and complaints from the public, adding that he has asked the Digital Policy Office to continue leading 1823 in adopting innovative technologies to drive efficiency.

 

Mr Lee said the current-term Government remains committed to translating policy blueprints into tangible outcomes that develop the economy and improve livelihoods. He emphasised that direct community exchanges are vital for understanding public needs, adding that the insights gained will help formulate upcoming policy initiatives as he and his team continue to listen to views from all sectors of society.

Three logistics solutions approved
body:
The Government today announced a first batch of three preapproved information technology onboarding solutions under the Future Innovative Logistics Acceleration Scheme.

 

Eligible third-party logistics service providers can now apply for funding support in subscribing to or using these solutions. Individual enterprises can receive funding support of up to $2million.

 

Twenty-six applications were received after providers were earlier invited to apply for their IT onboarding solutions to be included on a white list of preapproved solutions under the scheme.

 

The Hong Kong Productivity Council (HKPC), the Logistics & Supply Chain MultiTech R&D Centre and the Airport Authority assessed the applications based on their compatibility with relevant logistics data platforms, functionality, usability, security and project management planning. The three highest-scoring solutions were selected for the first batch of preapproved solutions to be included on the white list.

 

The Transport & Logistics Bureau said that digitalisation is a key priority for the logistics industry to maintain its competitiveness.

 

With the availability of preapproved solutions under the scheme, the bureau hopes that service provides will seize the opportunity to digitalise their businesses and explore the benefits offered by logistics data platforms including greater logistics transparency, more efficient supply chain management and trade financing opportunities.

 

Details of the pilot scheme and relevant application materials are available on its dedicated website. Interested service providers can call 2788 6077 or email the HKPC.

title: 3rd InnoHK research cluster launched
body:
The Innovation & Technology Commission today held a launch ceremony for the third InnoHK research cluster, SEAM@InnoHK, which focuses on four frontier technology fields: sustainable development, energy, advanced manufacturing and materials.

 

Eight research centres have been approved for admission to SEAM@InnoHK, receiving total government funding support of around $2.5 billion. Led by renowned local and overseas universities and research institutions, these centres have established collaborations with top-tier partners from the Chinese Mainland and worldwide, creating a network that includes the UK, France, the Netherlands, Switzerland and Japan.

 

Speaking at the launch ceremony, Secretary for Innovation, Technology & Industry Prof Sun Dong said that the research of the eight research centres spans next-generation semiconductors, sustainable energy, innovative materials, space manufacturing, advanced manufacturing technologies and smart energy management. He noted that the initiative echoes the call to drive high-end manufacturing, accelerate growth of strategic emerging industries, and deepen the green transition under the National 15th Five-Year Plan.

 

Prof Sun added that by integrating advanced technologies into local industries, the third research cluster demonstrates the Government's unwavering commitment to promoting real-world applications of research outcomes to accelerate Hong Kong's development into an international innovation and technology (I&T) centre.

 

The participating institutions include many of the world's top 100 universities and research and development institutes in frontier technology fields. This demonstrates Hong Kong's unique advantage as a “super connector” to seamlessly bridge top-tier international academic resources with local industrial needs.

 

Currently, the eight research centres are preparing to set up their laboratories and will come into operation progressively to inject new momentum into Hong Kong's I&T ecosystem. As a flagship international I&T initiative of the Government, InnoHK aims to bring together world-class institutions and local universities to establish premier research centres in the city.
